summary.headline: Vimta Q2 FY27 total income up 9.9% YoY to INR1,149 mn, EBITDA margin 35.5%, PAT up only 3.5% YoY; sequential revenue flat on pharma and food lull.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total income rose 9.9% YoY to INR1,149 million, with EBITDA up 10.5% to INR408 million at a 35.5% margin. Management said revenue was broadly flat QoQ, citing longer pharma customer decision cycles and a food-sample slowdown linked to Middle East disruption. PAT grew only 3.5% YoY to INR206 million (17.9% margin), with gross margin dipping on added capacity and higher material consumption. H1 FY27 total income was INR2,278 million (+11.8%), EBITDA INR819 million (+13.2%, 36% margin) and PAT INR417 million (+7.3%). The company remains net debt-free, with cash of INR701 million after taking INR15 crore of new long-term borrowing.

segments.name: Preclinical
segments.commentary: Management says it is among the largest growth drivers, with ~30% CAGR over the last four years; large-animal facility capacity constraint hit in H1 and is being expanded. Discovery work is mostly exports; safety/impurity work ~30-35%, all domestic.

segments.name: Clinical research (CRADS / BA/BE)
segments.commentary: Clinical research was weak in FY26 after losing major clients; BA/BE capacity fixed at 180 beds by choice. Contracts now with multiple customers; lead times 12-18 months; improvement expected in Q3-Q4. CT (clinical trials) had a lull after one large study.

segments.name: Biologics services
segments.commentary: Revenue generation began in Q2 FY27 with an initial booked order; revenue still very modest. About INR20-25 crore invested; talks with multiple clients, with management hoping to onboard a couple more this quarter. Ticket sizes INR100-125 lakh for process work; INR4-7 crore for lab-scale biosimilar development.

segments.name: Pharma analytics
segments.commentary: Top 5 or top 10 client share has ranged roughly 25-35% and varies by quarter; ~40% of pharma analytics revenue from overseas clients per slide. Management says large molecules are the future focus; peptides were strong last year.

segments.name: Food testing
segments.commentary: Export sample volumes fell sharply (e.g., 20-25 samples per shipment now down to 2-3). Import sample volumes at about 60-70% of normal, recovering from 30-40% in April-July. Shifting toward domestic clients.

segments.name: Electronics / EMI-EMC testing
segments.commentary: Stable QoQ with existing customers including defence OEMs, who use ~70-80% of Hyderabad capacity. EMI/EMC chamber capacity doubled after maxing utilisation; the business is small and volumes are episodic.

segments.name: Environment testing (PPM)
segments.commentary: Only PPM services offered; management will focus on higher-technology, higher-value PPM services.

guidance_outlook: No quarterly outlook given; management expects Q3 and Q4 to be better, with H2 typically stronger than H1.
Medium-term: management reiterates FY28 turnover of about INR700 crore with 35-36% EBITDA margin, equivalent to ~20-25% top-line CAGR, per analyst question and CEO confirmation.
EBITDA margin: no major shift in coming quarters; medium term a possible correction of 100-200 bps driven by service mix shift toward biologics, not input costs.
FY27 capex budget about INR80 crore (maintenance INR45-50 crore); management says H2 spend will be as planned after H1 underspend versus plan.
Food export/import sample recovery expected to normalise in Q3 or by Q4.
Biologics expected to reach a 1:1 asset-turn by year 3, possibly year 2; biologics could make a mark on top line within 2 years if opportunities materialise.
capex_capacity: Roughly INR100 crore building/lab infrastructure capex, built over ~2 years post-COVID, providing space for 5-7 years of growth; management says no new lab space needed for existing services for 5-7 years.
Biologics CRADS: ~INR20-25 crore invested; reactor-based capacity, with more reactors needed for expansion.
Preclinical: large-animal holding capacity is the binding constraint in H1 FY27; expansion under way.
EMI/EMC chamber capacity doubled in Hyderabad after utilisation was maxed out.
Capex H1 FY27 ran at about INR112-115 crore, above the INR80 crore FY27 plan; management says the underspend was not utilised as planned and H2 will follow plan.
Management says incremental capex would be in line with depreciation; no significant step-up expected.
demand_pricing: Management attributes flat QoQ revenue to a lull in pharma R&D pipelines (began in Q1), with RFP inflows picking up in recent months.
Food: export sample volumes sharply reduced as exporters change shipping strategies amid higher freight and insurance costs; Middle East war cited.
Gross margin dip attributed to new capacity under-absorption and slightly higher material consumption; no reclassification in P&L.
Employees ~1,400, flat over 2-3 years; FTE share under 5%. Employee cost ~28% of revenue in FY26 and management does not expect it to fall to 25-26%; productivity gains only offset wage inflation.
Competitive and regulatory headwinds noted: regulatory wait-and-watch on approvals; talent availability.
Industry tailwinds cited: pharma exports record USD31 bn in FY26 (~7% growth in Q1 FY27); electronics exports up ~39% this fiscal; EV registrations up ~90%; defence budget up.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue growth down to ~10% after INR100 crore capex, and what drove the gross margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth slowdown is external: pharma R&D lull and food sample decline. No reclassification; margin dip reflects added capacity and higher material consumption.

qa_highlights.question: Clinical research constraints and food testing domestic shift?
qa_highlights.answer: BA/BE capacity capped at 180 beds by choice; lost major clients last year, now multiple contracts with 12-18 month lead times. Food pivoted to domestic clients after export hit from Middle East war.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins of 35-36% hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Not significantly in coming quarters; medium term possible 100-200 bps correction from biologics service mix, not input costs.

qa_highlights.question: Biologics ticket sizes and capex payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Process work INR100-125 lakh (~$100-150k); lab-scale biosimilar development INR4-7 crore+. Target 1:1 asset turn on ~INR20 crore invested, likely year 3, possibly year 2.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company still stand by FY28 INR700 crore turnover and 35-36% margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management confirmed medium-term confidence; pharma R&D is temporarily slow and food disruption is temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Why borrow INR15 crore while holding ~INR70 crore cash, and is FY27 capex still INR80 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowing cheaper than using own cash and keeps liquidity for opportunities. H1 capex ran ~INR112-115 crore; H2 expected to follow plan.

risks_watch: Pharma R&D pipeline slowdown persisting beyond Q3-Q4; conversion of RFPs into executable projects is key.
Biologics revenue still negligible; ramp timeline of 2+ years and possible 100-200 bps margin dilution from mix.
Capex execution: H1 spend far above plan; H2 must align with INR80 crore budget. Asset turns remain low so far.
Food export/import sample recovery (from ~60-70% of normal) needs to reach normal levels by Q4.
ROE and ROCE declined YoY, attributed to a larger equity base and new debt; new long-term borrowing INR15 crore.
Client concentration: top 5-10 clients ~25-35% of pharma analytics revenue, varying quarter to quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term potential but cautious on near-term revenue; management attributes the flat sequential top line to external factors (pharma R&D lull, food sample disruption) and avoids quarterly guidance. Answers were sometimes evasive on capex utilisation and biologics economics, and the CEO said guidance rests on a 'coiled spring' thesis.
key_quotes: Overall, there is still growth, and I'm pretty optimistic that in the future, we will see better results.
So we are doing very good if we are able to offset it, and that's what we are experiencing so far.
Medium term, I think we are quite confident. If I may give an analogy for Vimta, it's like a coiled spring now.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No quarterly outlook given and the FY28 INR700 crore target was only reiterated, with Q2 growth at 9.9% and flat QoQ revenue.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 total income grew only 9.9% YoY and was flat QoQ, PAT grew 3.5%, and food export samples fell to 2-3 per shipment from 20-25, with pharma R&D lull persisting; FY28 INR700 crore target needs ~20-25% CAGR.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Biologics services generated first revenue in Q2 FY27 with one booked order, and management hopes to onboard a couple more clients this quarter at INR100-125 lakh process tickets and INR4-7 crore biosimilar lab-scale tickets.

rows.label: Clinical research (BA/BE) contract recovery
rows.why: Multiple new contracts with 12-18 month lead times and improvement expected in Q3-Q4 after losing major clients in FY26; BA/BE capacity capped at 180 beds.

rows.label: Food testing normalisation
